title: Removing an entry takes a comment indented under it and leaves the literal scalar before it alone
notes: The literal scalar of `k` ends at `  x: 1`, which is less indented than its content (production 173), so the value of `k` is `v` and one line break. `    # c` follows `x: 1` and is indented under it: it is a comment (section 6.6) and the lines of a block scalar before it are not touched by it. Removing `/a/x` takes the entry and, by the kit convention for comments (docs/edit-semantics.md, Comments: 'A comment line directly after an entry and indented more than its key belongs to that entry and goes with it'), the comment; YAML gives comments no owner, hence the tags. The comment must not become content of the literal scalar of `k`: the value of `k` stays `v\n`, and `b: 2` stays.

provenance.reference: A patch engine that moved the comment line into the preceding block scalar, or kept it, after the entry it belonged to was removed.
